newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trustor says Lord Moyne buys 17 pct of it.
newsitem.headline: Trustor says Lord Moyne buys 17 pct of it.

text.p: Swedish investment company Trustor said on Tuesday Lord Moyne had bought 17 percent of capital and 52 percent of votes in the group.

Lord Moyne, formerly Jonathan Guinness, of the brewery family Guinness, had bought the stake from Trustor chief executive Per-Olov Norberg, who will step down from his post, the company said in a statement.

The deal is conditional on Norberg being allowed to buy Trustor's shares in electrical heating appliance group Kanthal for about 700 million crowns in cash, corresponding to 190 crowns a share, the company said.
Kanthal closed at 210 crowns on Friday, the last day of trading before the Whitsun holiday when markets were closed.
Norberg, who will remain Kanthal's chairman, will thereby become the new main owner of the electrical heating appliance group with 29 percent of capital and 49.9 percent of votes.
"Trustor will go back to being a diversified investment company with holdings mainly in listed Nordic shares," Lord Moyne said.
"In addition, we plan to suggest strategic investments in Nordic growth companies."
"With its new direction, Trustor should be able to give a return on capital invested to its shareholders at a significantly higher level than during the past years," he said.
"The dividend level should be at least in line with the average on the Stockholm Stock Exchange."
